questions: Verify print mode, no-session-persistence, structured schema, tool restrictions and resume flags.
Measure subscription quota separately from API cash and cache write/read economics.
decision: Keep the Claude CLI adapter as the compatibility reference, add versioned capability fixtures and least-privilege role profiles, and evaluate SDK/native workflows only behind an explicit adapter boundary.
code_observations: build_worker_command uses Claude print mode with disabled session persistence; a subsequent fresh process cannot be assumed to remember the previous attempt.
The runner has separate worker and summary command builders. A read-only summary must remain a restricted command path rather than a general implementation worker with a polite prompt.

symbols.name: ## Elevation mechanics (how a route is actually obtained)

implementation_steps: Add recorded help/version fixtures and a capability map for the exact installed Claude CLI. Probe flags non-generatively and fail visibly on unsupported combinations.
Preserve fresh-context defaults. Separate optional resume/session-retention experiments from normal execution and document that conversation persistence does not snapshot source files.
Test structured report extraction, schema rejection, malformed envelopes and nonzero statuses separately. A valid JSON shape cannot replace deterministic product validation.
Qualify read-only paths with an actual tool allowlist/sandbox boundary and clean environment, including third-party endpoint profiles.
Capture available usage fields in native units, retaining null for absent values. Do not equate subscription tokens with API invoices or assume a universal cache rate.
Pin documented CLI capabilities by version and fail on unsupported security or structured-output options.
Test review tool inheritance and source-revision isolation rather than trusting a read-only prompt.
Compare SDK or native workflows with CLI execution only after lifecycle, billing and validation equivalence checks.
proposed_acceptance_tests: Default worker argv retains no-session-persistence and existing approved permission behavior.
Summary mode cannot write a planted repository file or execute an unapproved mutating tool in a supported test environment.
Invalid JSON, missing report fields, quota errors and semantic failures take different paths.
A model alias mapped through another endpoint is reported with host and backend identity.
Unknown usage is null and no secret environment values enter diagnostics.
A partial max-turn result cannot complete a task.
No-session-persistence does not trigger an automatic resume attempt.
Unsupported permission restrictions fail closed without global settings changes.
A restricted reviewer cannot invoke inherited write tools.

cost_model: Preserve the working CLI unless SDK startup/cache savings exceed migration, maintenance and review costs at equal outcome quality. Record subscription and API costs separately.

previous_decision: Keep the Claude CLI adapter thin and version-qualified, with explicit session, schema, permission and usage contracts.
revision_delta: The research adds worktree starting-revision risk, tool inheritance and version-specific budget/session semantics. A native SDK migration is not presumed to be a cost-saving rewrite.
decision_analysis: The existing ephemeral headless worker is a useful portable contract. Keep exact argv fixtures and parse final result, partial result and usage separately. Unsupported flags must fail preflight with an actionable compatibility reason rather than being silently dropped or replaced with a more permissive mode.

A review or observer role needs an actual restricted tool/sandbox boundary. A prompt saying read-only is not enforcement; inherited tools and project settings can broaden access. Give the worker only assigned context and record actual CLI/model identity. A claimed maximum tier is not evidence that the requested native effort was used.

Native subagents, SDK sessions and forks can reduce repeated setup or share cached context, but they add distinct lifecycle and persistence contracts. Keep them optional until they preserve cancellation, independent validation, retry accounting and source revision. The relevant comparison is end-to-end validated cost against the existing CLI, not fewer lines of orchestration code.

Budget and persistence options should be per invocation and documented by supported version. Do not alter user-global configuration as a convenience. Keep secrets in environment references, record neither values nor raw authentication traces, and do not convert a subscription login into API billing automatically.
